ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, point $D$ is on line $AC$, connecting $BD$. If $\angle DBC=45^\circ$, what is the maximum value of $\frac{AD}{CD}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, construct the circumcircle of $\triangle BCD$, denoted as $\odot O$. Construct $OE \perp AC$ at point E, and $OF \perp AB$ at point F, and connect OB,\\
$\because \angle AEO = \angle AFO = \angle BAC = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral OFAE is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$ AE=OF,\\
$\because DE=CE= \frac{1}{2}CD$,\\
$\therefore$ CD=2CE,\\
The lengths of CD, CE remain constant. When OF is at its maximum, then AE is at its maximum, and thus AD is at its maximum,\\
$\therefore$ the value of $\frac{AD}{CD}$ is also at its maximum,\\
$\because OF \leq OB$,\\
$\therefore$ when OF=OB, OF is at its maximum,\\
At this time, point B coincides with point F,\\
As shown in Figure 2, when point B coincides with point F, connect OD and OC,\\
Let DE=CE=m, then CD=2m,\\
$\because \angle DBC=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DOC=2\angle DBC=90^\circ$,\\
$\because OD=OC$,\\
$\therefore OE= \frac{1}{2}CD=DE=m$,\\
$\therefore AE=OB=OD= \sqrt{DE^2+OE^2}=\sqrt{m^2+m^2}=\sqrt{2}m$,\\
$\therefore AD=AE−DE= \sqrt{2}m−m$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AD}{CD}=\frac{\sqrt{2}m−m}{2m}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}−1}{2}}$.

推理：设 β=∠ABC。因为 ∠DBC=45°，所以 ∠ABD=β−45°。又因为 ∠BAC=90°，所以 ∠ACB=90°−β；由于 D 在 AC 上，故在三角形 BCD 中，∠BCD=90°−β。

在直角三角形 ABD 中，由正弦关系得 AD/BD=sin(β−45°)。

在三角形 BCD 中，由正弦定理，CD/BD=sin45°/sin(90°−β)=1/(√2 cosβ)。

因此 AD/CD = [AD/BD]/[CD/BD] = √2 cosβ·sin(β−45°)。展开 sin(β−45°)=(sinβ−cosβ)/√2，得 AD/CD=cosβ(sinβ−cosβ)。令 t=tanβ，因为 β>45°，所以 t>1。于是 AD/CD=(t−1)/(1+t²)。

最大化 f(t)=(t−1)/(1+t²)，t>1。求导得 f'(t)=[1+t²−2t(t−1)]/(1+t²)²=(1+2t−t²)/(1+t²)²。令 1+2t−t²=0，得 t=1+√2。此时取得最大值：f(1+√2)=√2/[1+(1+√2)²]=√2/(4+2√2)=(√2−1)/2。
method.answer_match_reason: The predicted answer matches the standard maximum value exactly: (√2−1)/2.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, point $D$ is on line $AC$, connecting $BD$. If $\angle DBC=45^\circ$, what is the maximum value of $\frac{AD}{CD}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, construct the circumcircle of $\triangle BCD$, denoted as $\odot O$. Construct $OE \perp AC$ at point E, and $OF \perp AB$ at point F, and connect OB,\\
$\because \angle AEO = \angle AFO = \angle BAC = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral OFAE is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$ AE=OF,\\
$\because DE=CE= \frac{1}{2}CD$,\\
$\therefore$ CD=2CE,\\
The lengths of CD, CE remain constant. When OF is at its maximum, then AE is at its maximum, and thus AD is at its maximum,\\
$\therefore$ the value of $\frac{AD}{CD}$ is also at its maximum,\\
$\because OF \leq OB$,\\
$\therefore$ when OF=OB, OF is at its maximum,\\
At this time, point B coincides with point F,\\
As shown in Figure 2, when point B coincides with point F, connect OD and OC,\\
Let DE=CE=m, then CD=2m,\\
$\because \angle DBC=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DOC=2\angle DBC=90^\circ$,\\
$\because OD=OC$,\\
$\therefore OE= \frac{1}{2}CD=DE=m$,\\
$\therefore AE=OB=OD= \sqrt{DE^2+OE^2}=\sqrt{m^2+m^2}=\sqrt{2}m$,\\
$\therefore AD=AE−DE= \sqrt{2}m−m$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AD}{CD}=\frac{\sqrt{2}m−m}{2m}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}−1}{2}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a right triangle ABC, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the upper right, AB vertical, AC horizontal, and ∠BAC a right angle. Point D is located on AC and close to A, and BD and BC are connected in the figure.

Reasoning: According to the method, set coordinates A=(0,0), C=(1,0), B=(0,b), D=(d,0), where 0<d<1. From ∠DBC=45°, consider the two straight lines BD and BC starting from B. Their slopes respectively correspond to vectors BD=(d,-b), BC=(1,-b). Using the tangent formula for the angle between two straight lines, tan∠DBC=1, so
b(1-d)/(d+b^2)=1.
Therefore b(1-d)=d+b^2, and after rearranging, d(1+b)=b-b^2, so
 d=b(1-b)/(1+b).
Thus
AD/CD=d/(1-d)=[b(1-b)/(1+b)]/[1-b(1-b)/(1+b)]=b(1-b)/(1+b^2).
Let f(b)=b(1-b)/(1+b^2), 0<b<1. Differentiating gives
f'(b)=(1-2b-b^2)/(1+b^2)^2.
Let f'(b)=0, obtaining b^2+2b-1=0, so b=√2-1. At the endpoints the function tends to 0, so this critical point gives the maximum value.
Substituting gives
f(√2-1)=(√2-1)/2.
The final maximum value is (√2-1)/2.
